environmentNotes: Free-text notes passed into every check's prompt (shared resources, do-not-restart services, temp file locations, etc.).

checks.name: example-fast-check
checks.module: Runs every time, iterative or final (finalOnly absent = always run)
checks.instructions: Fix the root cause of any failure; do not weaken assertions to make it pass.

checks.name: example-explicit-always-check
checks.module: Same as above, but explicit about it
checks.instructions: Fix the root cause of any failure.

checks.name: example-slow-check
checks.module: Only runs on the final verification pass (finalRun: true)
checks.instructions: Slow/expensive check — skip on every iterative pass, run once before declaring done.

checks.name: example-grouped-check-a
checks.module: group = the concurrency unit: different groups run at the SAME time, checks inside one group run IN ORDER. Put every check that touches the same shared mutable resource (a real DB, a running dev server, a build output others consume) in one group.
checks.instructions: Fix the root cause of any failure.

checks.name: example-grouped-check-b
checks.module: Same group as the check above, so it is guaranteed never to run at the same time as it. If this one's predecessor fails unfixably, this check is skipped and reported in the result's `skipped` list.
checks.instructions: Fix the root cause of any failure.

checks.name: example-independent-check
checks.module: A different group, so it runs concurrently with the shared-db group. Checks that only READ sources (lint, in-process unit tests) belong here. A check with no `group` at all falls into a shared `_default` group, i.e. fully serial — which is what a config written before this field existed expects.
checks.instructions: Fix the root cause of any failure.

checks.name: example-timeout-check
checks.module: timeoutSeconds caps the single foreground call that runs this check; past it the command is killed and reported as a timed-out failure instead of hanging. Max 600 (the Bash tool's ceiling).
checks.instructions: Fix the root cause of any failure. A timeout usually points to the process not exiting after finishing its work (e.g. an unclosed DB connection or uncleared timer), not a real test regression — check the output collected before the kill.
